scenario: round(x) is nearest-integer with ties-to-even (Python banker's rounding) per LEXP.3.2, returning Int. Each tie lands on the even neighbour: round(2.5)==2 (not 3) and round(3.5)==4; round(2.6)==3 is the ordinary nearest case. 2.5 and 3.5 are exact dyadic floats so each tie is genuine. The round(2.5)==2 rule is the discriminator — an away-from-zero impl computes 3 and fails to fire it.
rules_ds:
schema T scope logical:
    a: Float key
    b: Float mutable
    c: Float mutable

rule r_round_tie_even_down:
    T t where round(t.a) == 2
->
    log critical "a"

rule r_round_tie_even_up:
    T t where round(t.b) == 4
->
    log critical "b"

rule r_round_ordinary:
    T t where round(t.c) == 3
->
    log critical "c"
